newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat, King Hussein meet over Hebron impasse.
newsitem.headline: Arafat, King Hussein meet over Hebron impasse.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat held talks in Amman with Jordan's King Hussein on Monday and accused Israel of failing to honour long-delayed peace accords.

"There are a lot of difficulties, they are not intending to implement accurately and honestly what had been agreed upon and what had been signed," he said after visiting a Jordan hospital treating Palestinians injured in recent Israeli-Palestinian violence.

Palestinians have been angered by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's delay in implementing an agreement on pulling back Israeli troops in Hebron, signed by the previous Israeli government a year ago.
Palestinian spokesman Nabil Abu-Rudainah told Reuters that U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross would meet Arafat in the Jordanian capital later on Monday night to help break the impasse.
Officials confirmed Dennis Ross had arrived and the meeting had begun with the presence of King Hussein.
Earlier a senior PLO official in Jerusalem said King Hussein would travel to the West Bank on Tuesday with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for his first visit to the region in 29 years.
King Hussein has not visited the West Bank since Israel seized the territory from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war.

Asked about the outcome of his talks earlier in the day with King Hussein, Arafat said: "We explained to His Majesty the difficulties we are facing in our talks with the Israelis and we agreed to follow these issues with each other."

Arafat, brushing aside questions about a possible meeting with the Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, said: "The most important thing is not the meeting...the most important thing is the implementation of what has been agreed."

PLO officials said Arafat had rejected a proposal by Netanyahu that they could hold a summit on Monday if Arafat agreed to change the Hebron deal and give Israel powers in areas that were to go to the PLO.

Jordan state television said King Hussein, in a telephone call to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, stressed "the need to continue with the peace process and exert efforts to overcome obstacles facing it".
King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab ally since Jordan signed a peace treaty in 1994, has stepped up public support of Arafat in recent days while distancing himself from Netanyahu.
He called on Sunday for a speedy implementation of the Hebron troop redeployment.
"Peace was in jeopardy and still is, unless these negotiations lead to concrete and conclusive results," the monarch said after returning from a trip to London.

Worried Jordanian officials say recent violence in Palestinian territories raised the danger of chaos on the West Bank spilling over into the kingdom because of close demographic, political and economic links.
